title: Run machine who turned loyalty into a legacy at Bengaluru
clues: Indian batting superstar and the long-time talisman of Royal Challengers Bangalore.
Holds the mantle as the IPL’s all-time leading run-scorer.
Authored the greatest single-season haul with 973 runs in 2016.
Claimed the Orange Cap twice, in 2016 and 2024.
Has eight IPL centuries and has spent his entire IPL career with RCB.

title: The calm conductor behind a five‑title Chennai dynasty
clues: Indian wicketkeeper-batter renowned for ice-cold finishing and leadership.
Long-time skipper of Chennai Super Kings (CSK), with a two-season stint at the Rising Pune franchise during CSK’s suspension (2016–17).
First cricketer to appear in 250 IPL matches.
Holds the IPL records for most wicketkeeper dismissals and most stumpings.
Captained CSK to five championships (2010, 2011, 2018, 2021, 2023) and was the costliest buy at the inaugural 2008 auction at US$1.5 million.

title: Slinging yorkers that decided a title by a single run
clues: Sri Lankan pace ace famed for a slinging action and relentless toe-crushers.
Became a Mumbai Indians stalwart across four championship-winning seasons.
Claimed the 2011 Purple Cap with 28 wickets in a single campaign.
Long-time IPL leading wicket-taker, finishing with 170 scalps for one franchise.
Sealed the 2019 final with a last-ball LBW to Shardul Thakur, clinching a one-run win over Chennai.

title: Death-overs maestro with a record purple patch
clues: West Indian seam-bowling all-rounder famed for death-overs variations and celebratory flair.
Key figure for Chennai Super Kings across multiple titles, after earlier IPL seasons with Mumbai Indians and a stint at Gujarat Lions.
One of the first to win the Purple Cap twice, topping the wicket charts in 2013 and 2015.
Set a single-season benchmark with 32 wickets in 2013, a tally that stands as a joint IPL record.
Retired as the league’s all-time leading wicket-taker with 183 scalps, later surpassed by newer leaders.

title: Spin enigma turned opening firecracker for a purple powerhouse
clues: West Indian all-rounder famed for ‘mystery’ spin and explosive powerplay hitting.
A Kolkata Knight Riders mainstay since 2012, central to title wins in 2012, 2014, and 2024.
Only player to be named IPL Most Valuable Player three times (2012, 2018, 2024).
In 2024, produced a rare double: 488 runs and 17 wickets — first in IPL history with 400+ runs and 15+ wickets in a single season.
Holds KKR’s fastest fifty — 15 balls vs RCB at Bengaluru in 2017 — and has 150+ IPL wickets with a career economy under 7.

title: The auction splurge that paid back with twin trophies.
clues: Indian left-handed opener renowned for gritty intent and sharp T20 leadership.
Rose to prominence in the league’s early years with Delhi before redefining a Kolkata side’s fortunes.
Became the most expensive purchase at the 2011 auction and was handed the captaincy immediately.
Amassed 4,000+ IPL runs without a century, logging a personal best of 93 and a stack of fifties.
Captained Kolkata to IPL titles in 2012 and 2014, cementing a new powerhouse era.

title: Three Orange Caps and a title to match
clues: Explosive left‑handed Australian opener who terrorized powerplays for over a decade.
Became the first overseas batter to cross 5000 IPL runs, long the league’s top foreign run‑getter.
The only player with three Orange Caps in IPL history (2015, 2017, 2019).
Captained Sunrisers Hyderabad to their maiden IPL title in 2016, scoring 848 runs that season.
Starred for Delhi Daredevils/Capitals and Sunrisers Hyderabad; missed the 2018 IPL due to a ball‑tampering ban.

title: The hat-trick habit no batter enjoys
clues: Indian leg-spinner who has featured in the league since the inaugural 2008 season.
Represented Delhi (Daredevils/Capitals), Deccan Chargers, Sunrisers Hyderabad, and Lucknow Super Giants.
Among the IPL’s top wicket-takers, comfortably past the 150-wicket mark.
Only bowler with three IPL hat-tricks, achieved in 2008, 2011, and 2013.
Produced a 5/17 masterclass for Delhi in 2008 in a match that included his hat-trick.

title: Clutch all-rounder who turns tight finishes into headlines
clues: Indian all-rounder famed for left-arm orthodox spin, left-handed batting, and lightning fielding.
An inaugural-season winner with Rajasthan, a long-time cornerstone of Chennai, and a stopover with Gujarat Lions in 2016–17.
Smashed a record 37 runs in a single IPL over in 2021—off Purple Cap holder Harshal Patel against RCB.
Delivered a rare IPL all-round masterclass in 2012 vs Deccan Chargers: 48 off 29 and 5/16 for Chennai.
Sealed the 2023 final in Ahmedabad with 10 off the last two balls (6 and 4 off Mohit Sharma) to win the title for Chennai.

title: The Big-Hitting West Indian Who Broke T20 Records
clues: Towering West Indian batter and part-time off-spinner who dominated the IPL for over a decade.
Started with Kolkata Knight Riders before becoming a superstar at Royal Challengers Bangalore, later starring for Kings XI/Punjab Kings.
Holds the IPL records for highest individual score (175* in 2013) and fastest century (30 balls).
All-time league leader in sixes and once smashed 17 maximums in a single innings.
Won the Orange Cap twice (2011, 2012) and was the 2011 Player of the Tournament.

title: The early-era enforcer who twice swung Kolkata’s title dreams
clues: Indian all-rounder famed for brutal middle-order hitting and handy off-spin.
Starred for Rajasthan Royals before becoming a key finisher at Kolkata Knight Riders; later played for Sunrisers Hyderabad.
Collected three IPL titles across two teams: RR (2008) and KKR (2012, 2014).
Blasted a 37-ball century for RR against Mumbai Indians in 2010, among the league’s quickest hundreds.
Took 3/22 and smashed 56 in the 2008 final, earning Player of the Match as RR won the inaugural title.

title: Back-to-back Purple Caps and a death-overs surgeon
clues: Indian swing-bowling spearhead known for new-ball movement and calm death-overs spells.
Represented Pune Warriors India before becoming Sunrisers Hyderabad’s long-time pace leader.
First player to win consecutive IPL Purple Caps, topping the charts in 2016 and 2017.
Claimed two five-wicket hauls in the 2017 season, a rare feat in the league.
Instrumental in Sunrisers Hyderabad’s 2016 title run, finishing as the season’s leading wicket-taker.

title: Four tons in one summer from the Royals’ English spark plug
clues: Explosive English opener–keeper renowned for 360-degree strokeplay in T20s.
Featured for Mumbai Indians before becoming a top-order mainstay at Rajasthan Royals.
Strung together five consecutive fifties in 2018, igniting a late-season surge for RR.
Dominated 2022 with the Orange Cap and MVP, blasting 863 runs and four hundreds.
Shares the IPL single-season hundreds record (4), achieved during that 2022 campaign.

title: Leg-spin maestro who topped the charts after switching sides
clues: Indian leg-spinner renowned for dismantling batting line-ups in the middle overs.
Starred for Royal Challengers Bangalore from 2014–2021 before joining Rajasthan Royals in 2022.
Secured the Purple Cap in 2022 with 27 wickets, a campaign that also featured a hat-trick.
Became the first bowler to reach 200 IPL wickets during the 2024 season.
Recorded 5/40 and a match-sealing hat-trick against Kolkata Knight Riders at Brabourne in 2022.

title: Made for the Big Stage
clues: Australian allrounder who twice claimed the IPL’s Player of the Tournament (2008 and 2013).
A cornerstone of Rajasthan Royals’ maiden 2008 title run, later a big-match star for Chennai Super Kings.
Among the select few with four IPL centuries, including two in a single season (2018).
Joined the rare club of 3000+ runs and 90+ wickets in the league.
Blasted 117* in the 2018 final to deliver CSK the trophy.

title: The first to 5,000 IPL runs and the heartbeat of Chennai’s dynasty.
clues: Indian left-handed batter renowned for relentless consistency and athletic fielding.
A long-time pillar of Chennai Super Kings, he also captained Gujarat Lions during CSK’s 2016–2017 hiatus.
Registered 400+ runs in seven consecutive seasons (2008–2014), setting the early benchmark for reliability.
Smashed a blistering 87 off 25 balls in the 2014 playoffs—an all-time knockout classic.
Became the first player to reach 5,000 IPL runs in 2019 and is widely known as “Mr. IPL.”

title: Boundary bully who made a rare IPL double feel routine
clues: Indian left-handed opener who has featured in the tournament since its inaugural 2008 season.
Has represented Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Punjab in the league, including captaining the Mohali-based side.
Among the top three all-time IPL run-scorers and the tournament’s all-time leader in fours.
Became the first player to smash back-to-back IPL centuries, doing so in 2020 for Delhi.
Won the 2016 title with Sunrisers Hyderabad and is affectionately nicknamed “Gabbar.”

title: The engine room of a purple dynasty
clues: South African all-rounder renowned for classical batting and canny seam bowling in the IPL.
Starred for Royal Challengers Bangalore before becoming a cornerstone for Kolkata Knight Riders.
Stacked up 572 runs in the 2010 season, spending long stretches in the Orange Cap lead before finishing runner-up.
Key contributor to KKR’s title triumphs in 2012 and 2014, later returning on their coaching staff.
Finished his IPL career with 2,427 runs and 65 wickets across 98 matches.

title: From zero to hero, led the charge overseas
clues: Australian wicketkeeper-batter famed for explosive T20 starts and sharp glovework.
Captained a side to the 2009 IPL title during the season held in South Africa.
Starred for Deccan Chargers before later leading Kings XI Punjab.
Blasted 109* off 47 balls in 2008 against Mumbai Indians, among the league’s earliest centuries.
In 2013, rolled his arm over for a rare cameo and claimed his only IPL wicket by dismissing Harbhajan Singh.

title: The thunderous finisher who turned late overs into launchpads
clues: Jamaican power-hitting all‑rounder renowned for game‑breaking cameos and hostile short spells.
Became a Kolkata Knight Riders mainstay after an early stint with Delhi Daredevils; part of KKR’s title-winning squads in 2014 and 2024.
One of the few to win multiple IPL MVP awards, clinching the honor in 2015 and again in 2019.
Produced a historic 2019 season: 510 runs at a strike rate of 204.81 with 52 sixes, plus double‑digit wickets.
Holds the best career IPL strike rate among players with 1,000+ runs (170+ range), including a highest score of 88* for KKR.
